source: Output of AppFlowy Web's src/application/mcp/setup.ts and setupPrompt.ts for these server URLs. Regenerate with UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 (see setupGolden.test.ts) and copy to Desktop.

https://mcp.appflowy.com/mcp.promptWithPage:
Set up the AppFlowy MCP server so you can work with my AppFlowy workspace (AppFlowy setup prompt v1).

Server URL: https://mcp.appflowy.com/mcp
It uses Streamable HTTP with OAuth sign-in in my browser. There is no API key, and you never need my AppFlowy password.

1. Add the server to the app you are running in, named "appflowy". Use the first option that fits:
   - Claude Code: run `claude mcp add --transport http appflowy https://mcp.appflowy.com/mcp`. Add `--scope user` to make it available in every project.
   - Codex: run `codex mcp add appflowy --url https://mcp.appflowy.com/mcp`, then `codex mcp login appflowy`.
   - Gemini CLI: run `gemini mcp add --transport http appflowy https://mcp.appflowy.com/mcp`, then `/mcp auth appflowy`.
   - VS Code: run `code --add-mcp '{"name":"appflowy","type":"http","url":"https://mcp.appflowy.com/mcp"}'`.
   - Cursor: add {"mcpServers":{"appflowy":{"url":"https://mcp.appflowy.com/mcp"}}} to ~/.cursor/mcp.json.
   - Windsurf or Antigravity: add {"mcpServers":{"appflowy":{"serverUrl":"https://mcp.appflowy.com/mcp"}}} to the app's MCP config (mcp_config.json).
   - Another app that supports remote MCP servers: add a Streamable HTTP server with the URL above. An app that only runs local (stdio) servers can use `npx -y mcp-remote https://mcp.appflowy.com/mcp`.
   - Claude or ChatGPT, or any app whose configuration you can't change: don't guess. Tell me to add a custom connector (Claude) or app (ChatGPT) with the URL above, and point me to https://appflowy.com/oauth/mcp/setup for step-by-step instructions.
2. Start the sign-in and ask me to finish it in my browser: I sign in to AppFlowy, choose a workspace and approve access. If AppFlowy says the app needs approval, tell me to select Request approval and to try again once a workspace owner approves it.
3. Confirm the connection: call the AppFlowy get-self tool and tell me the name and email it returns. The connection covers the one workspace I chose; to use another one too, add the server again under another name, such as appflowy-work.
